bandReport.notes:
29 questions, 66-94 continuous, no gaps. Printed pages 25, 27, 29, 31, 33 (odd-numbered English pages; the facing even pages carry the Hindi text and show through as faint bleed-through only). Per-page split: p12 = 66-70, p13 = 71-76, p14 = 77-84, p15 = 85-89, p16 = 90-94.

Band edges checked against neighbouring territory: p11 (B2's last page) ends with BOTH columns closing on a complete option (d) — 'New Delhi' left, 'Reduction in the cash reserve ratio (CRR)' right — so nothing spills into p12 and Q66 is a clean fresh start. p17 (B4's first page) opens with Q95 left column and Q98 right column, so Q94 is the last question of my band and it completes in full on p16 (its option (d) ends '...transferable vote is followed.'). No question straddles either band boundary.

Option-order hazards found and verified at 8x rather than read once: Q69's code options are printed in NON-ascending order — (a) 1 and 3 only, (b) 2 and 3 only, (c) 1 only, (d) 1, 2 and 3 — i.e. the '1 only' single-statement option sits at (c), not at (a). No 'How many of the above statements' count-option item appears in this band. Q75 and Q91 are near-identical State/UT lists differing only by one or two names; both re-cropped at 8x and confirmed label-by-label. Q88's four planet groups likewise.

No page defects: no torn/occluded text, no missing option, no duplicated option, no misnumbering, no question with other than four options anywhere in the band.

Catalog gap (one, soft): Q84 asks who received the UNEP 'Champions of the Earth' award in the Entrepreneurial Vision category. This is an ENVIRONMENTAL award, but 'Current Affairs > Environment, Ecology and Energy' has no awards subtopic, and the nearest awards home, 'Awards, Honours, Books and Culture > Civilian Awards, Honours and Educational Institutions', reads as Padma-style civilian honours. Filed under the awards home and flagged on the question.

Two classification judgements worth recording for cross-band consistency, both applying the brief's structure-vs-event rule: (1) Q69 (PMSSY objectives) and Q72 (SWAYAM components) test a scheme's MANDATE rather than a dated announcement, but a scheme is not an institution with a subject home, and the catalog's only precise fits are 'Government Schemes, Policy and Governance > Health, Education and Welfare Schemes' — used for both. (2) Q71 (India's first all-woman UN peacekeeping contingent) is an armed-forces deployment, so it goes to 'Defence and Military Exercises > Armed Forces — Organisation, Commands and Operations' rather than to the National-milestones subtopic.
